subject.title: Org claim: vmware-aiops + vmware-monitor — @kingaiwork lookalikes impersonate @zw008 listings (same pattern as #2966/#3035)

question: After verifying the two production slug clusters, should authorized staff hard-delete the confirmed impersonator records and aliases that remain visible to publishing or scanning, rather than relying on a public-page hide?
rationale: The required action can destroy or reassign production registry records and must be based on staff-only ownership and moderation evidence; a read-only source review cannot safely authorize it.

options.title: Verify and fully remove collision records
options.body: Inspect both slug clusters, hard-delete only confirmed `@kingaiwork` orphan records and aliases that still participate in resolution, then prove scan and publish success for the legitimate listings.

options.title: Preserve records but repair lookup eligibility
options.body: Keep the disputed records for moderation retention while changing all relevant scan and resolution queries to exclude hidden or soft-deleted records, with a regression test for duplicate slugs.

recommendation.title: Verify and fully remove collision records
recommendation.body: Inspect both slug clusters, hard-delete only confirmed `@kingaiwork` orphan records and aliases that still participate in resolution, then prove scan and publish success for the legitimate listings.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged claim-intake work is the strongest available repository-history connection to the moderation path; an authorized moderation operator should make the final production-record decision.
